extracted.intended_audience: explorers, naturalists, and readers/authors of travel/exploration narratives
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, practices, and descriptive conventions used in a 19th‑century river exploration narrative — including surveying/navigation procedures, specimen collection, naming conventions, and vivid scene description. Useful for writers recreating or evaluating exploration accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect soundings and chart data
rubrics_metrics.description: "All the soundings and other data for the chart, in the immediate neighbourhood, were collected by the 16th..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gather complete local hydrographic measurements (soundings, channels, banks) before moving the ship; compile material for charts and local surveying. The surrounding text makes clear this is a preparatory, necessary step prior to further navigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anchor only where tide/depth permit (minimum depth requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: "we were obliged at that time to have at least seven fathoms."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose anchorage with sufficient depth to allow for great tidal falls; plan moves relative to tide heights. Context: anchoring mid‑channel was necessary because of a great fall of tide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use lead soundings and stream velocity to judge a river's importance
rubrics_metrics.description: "the lead gave a depth of eighteen and twenty fathoms, the velocity of the stream at the same time clearly showing how large a body of water was pouring through."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine depth measurements with observed current speed to assess whether an opening is likely the mouth of a major river and worth further exploration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assemble small boat parties with assigned roles for inshore exploration
rubrics_metrics.description: "It was soon arranged that Captain Wickham and myself, should at once dispel all doubts, and that next morning, Messrs. Fitzmaurice and Keys should start to explore..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize named parties (captain, officers, men) for reconnaissance: who goes where and when. The narrative uses clear delegation when launching exploratory excursions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision boats for short overland or river excursions
rubrics_metrics.description: "a few days provisions were stowed away in the boat"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carry limited provisions suited to small‑boat trips (a few days) when exploring upriver — plan supplies according to expected duration and difficulty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name geographical features by prominent impressions or persons
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: "we named River Peak"; "This is indeed a noble river!... at once bestowing upon it the name of Victoria River."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign toponyms based on distinguishing features, persons involved, or symbolic/honourific reasons; names also serve as navigational references (Leading Hill, Entrance Isle, Reach Hopeless).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use masthead and hill vantage points to trace channels and ranges
rubrics_metrics.description: "from the masthead, I could trace the low land forming the western side of the principal channel."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ascend masts or nearby hills early in daylight to map channels, observe ranges, and plan routes; repeated vantage observations are used to confirm courses and distances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take bearings and form 'leads' from aligned natural features
rubrics_metrics.description: "when the hill Captain Wickham and myself were first on, behind Entrance Isle, was in a line with the north end of the high land at the south side of the entrance, it formed a good lead up. In consequence we named it Leading Hill."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use line‑of‑sight alignments between hills/islets as navigational leads to guide boats through channels; record and name such aids on charts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess navigability by width, depth, shoals, and bends
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequent notes such as "width had hitherto been almost two miles, but there was not sufficient depth"; "the river ... much occupied by shoals"; "tortuous nature ... produces violent eddies and whirlpools."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether a waterway can carry a ship or only small boats by noting width, depth ranges (fathoms), frequency and location of shoals, and current/tidal behavior; record these for planning and charts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record precise measurements (distances, heights, compass bearings, fathoms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: "Endeavour Hill... afterwards found to be 690 feet"; "fresh about seventy miles above the ship"; many compass bearings and fathom depths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide numerical data (feet, miles, compass bearings, fathoms) to make descriptions operational for navigation and scientific record; used throughout as authoritative detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect natural history specimens and record descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions and specimen notes: alligator length and dentition, bird species (Geophaps plumifera, Nettapus pulchellas), fruit used for pie, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gather, kill if necessary, describe and preserve species (skins, specimens) with measurements and notes for later identification and illustration; note local abundance and behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leave memorials/records at visited sites
rubrics_metrics.description: "I left here a paper in a bottle, giving an account of our proceedings..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deposit written accounts or tokens at notable points as records of visit and directions for future parties; this is treated as a normal exploratory practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use local physical cues (soil, vegetation, fires) to infer habitability and native presence
rubrics_metrics.description: "the never‑failing eucalyptus... utterly sterile character"; "we saw fires of the natives"; "constant smoke near Indian Hill"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note vegetation type, soil horizon, and native signals (smoke, rafts) to infer fertility, flooding patterns, and human presence/communication networks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare for and respond to environmental hazards (whirlwinds, storms, mosquitoes, alligators)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accounts of whirlwinds nearly upsetting the gig, mosquitoes giving little rest, a thunderstorm that filled pools, and the killing/capture of an alligator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate local weather phenomena and fauna risks; carry appropriate precautions (anchoring, hauling boats ashore, defensive preparations) and adapt schedule (use rain to fill casks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ boat‑handling and portage techniques over shoals and flats
rubrics_metrics.description: "we had to drag the boats over the large flat that impeded our progress... plenty of rollers laid... an unlucky stone found its way through the thin plank of the gig."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use manpower, rollers, and temporary repairs to move boats across dry flats or shallow patches; accept slow, laborious progress and repair capability as necessary expedition skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use tides and channels strategically; prefer channel with better least water
rubrics_metrics.description: "one channel... the other... the least water is four fathoms, half a fathom more than was found in the other"; "the tides set direct through it, and to keep close to the bank is a simple and sure guide."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare alternate channels by minimum depth and tidal set; choose the channel with greater least depth and favorable tidal alignment and keep to local guides (banks, leads).

rubrics_metrics.name: Document and correct chronometer/instrument errors during shore observations
rubrics_metrics.description: "getting observations for the errors of the chronometers in the afternoon"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take shore observations to compute chronometer errors and correct navigation instruments as part of standard surveying practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name reaches and places to record emotional/experiential judgments
rubrics_metrics.description: Place names like "Long Reach", "Reach Hopeless", "Palm Island", "Station Hill" reflect observed character or expedition experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign informal names that encode practical or emotive information about a place (e.g., length, difficulty, features) to aid memory and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve valuable parts for transport and study (skins, best flesh, specimens)
rubrics_metrics.description: "we were some time skinning the monster, and after securing a little of the best part of the flesh for eating, proceeded on our way."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process large animals for preservation (skins) and consume or keep portions for food/scientific use; plan for transport back to ship for scientific cataloguing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine scientific observation with personal reflection and vivid scene-setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Passages of triumph and soliloquy: "the mingled emotions of that moment of triumph"; "to be the first civilized man that has ever trod on this spot" placed alongside careful geological and biological notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance technical/survey detail with emotive, sensory description to convey both factual information and the explorer's subjective experience — a stylistic convention of the genre evident throughout the text.
